title: ‘Blankety Blank,’ ‘Celebrity Mastermind’ & ‘Live At The Apollo’ All Canceled By The BBC Under Sweeping Content Cuts
full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake Agatha Christie Estate Posts Record Sales Amid Surging Film & TV Adaptations Benedict Cumberbatch Says Paramount-Warner Deal Is A “Calamity” That Must Be Blocked ‘The Deb’ Star Charlotte MacInnes Attacks Rebel Wilson In Appeal Against Court Defeat View All July 29, 2026 4:08am 'Blankety Blank' BBC The BBC has chopped a trio of entertainment shows under plans to save £500 million ($664M) over the coming years amid a funding crisis at the UK broadcaster. Blankety Blank , Celebrity Mastermind , and Live At The Apollo have all been canceled by the BBC, in what the corporation described as “difficult decisions.” “We are incredibly proud of all three of these much-loved shows and would like to thank everyone involved, both in front of and behind the camera, for bringing them to screen and making them such a success over many years,” the BBC said. Related Stories News Jared Leto Accused Of Criminal Sexual Conduct By Four Women In BBC Documentary News Agatha Christie Estate Posts Record Sales Amid Surging Film & TV Adaptations “Unfortunately, we have to make some really tough choices in light of our funding challenges, and these savings have been identified from the entertainment genre.” Watch on Deadline Blankety Blank first launched on British television in 1979, but was revived by the BBC in 2021 with Bradley Walsh on hosting duties. It is produced by Fremantle-owned Thames. Celebrity Mastermind is a spin-off of the iconic Mastermind quiz show. It first landed on the BBC as a special in 2002, before going on to air across 24 seasons. The format is owned by the BBC, but is produced on a contract by Hat Trick Productions, with Clive Myrie hosting. Celebrity Mastermind still has a series left to broadcast before it leaves the screen. Live at the Apollo is a 22-year-old stand-up comedy institution on the BBC. Launched in 2004, it has helped boost the careers of comics including Michael McIntyre and Alan Carr. The show is produced by Open Mike Productions and still has a series left to air on the BBC. The cuts form part of savings target of £100M for the BBC’s content division, which feeds into the wider £500M savings goal as fewer people pay the licence fee. The bigger picture behind the cuts is that 94% of the UK population use the BBC every month, but fewer than 80% pay the £180 annual licence fee. The BBC is attempting to bridge this gap. title: ‘The King’s Warden’ Leads Korea to Best First Half Box Office Since Pandemic
full_text: Jul 29, 2026 3:57am PT ‘The King’s Warden’ Leads Korea to Best First Half Box Office Since Pandemic By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest BTS Won’t Submit for 2027 Grammy Awards Consideration 4 hours ago Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Rajasthan Royals Sales Push IPL Cricket’s Business Value to $20.6 Billion, Houlihan Lokey Study Finds 4 hours ago How Lan Hongchun’s Teochew Film ‘Dear You’ Turned a Forgotten Postal Tradition Into China’s Unlikely Hit: ‘Dialect Is Never Going to Be a Liability as Long as You Have Great Ideas’ 20 hours ago See All BA Entertainment Local films drove Korean box office recovery in the first half of 2026, with total industry revenue reaching KRW579 billion ($399.1 million) on 57.05 million admissions, up 41.9% and 34.2% year-on-year, respectively, according to figures released by the Korean Film Council (KOFIC). Local titles accounted for the bulk of that growth. Korean-film revenue totaled KRW370.2 billion ($255.2 million) from 37.37 million admissions, an increase of 81.7% and 74.9% year-on-year. It is the strongest first-half showing for local cinema since the pandemic, with revenue now equivalent to 94.2% of the pre-pandemic first-half average calculated across 2017 to 2019. Admissions dropped 6.9% year-on-year, but revenue still rose 2.3%, a gain the council attributed to heavy premium-format ticket sales for titles including “ Project Hail Mary ” and “ Avatar: Fire and Ash .” Premium-format screenings made up 30.2% of total revenue for “Project Hail Mary” and 49.9% for “Avatar: Fire and Ash.” Popular on Variety “The King’s Warden” led all releases for the half, pulling in KRW163.1 billion ($112.4 million) from 16.91 million admissions to become the highest-grossing Korean film ever released. “ Colony ” ranked second with KRW60.5 billion ($41.7 million) from 5.74 million admissions, while “Salmokji: Whispering Water” placed third on KRW33.3 billion ($23 million) from 3.24 million admissions, giving Korean titles a clean sweep of the top three releases. KOFIC noted that strong results this half came not only from period dramas and action blockbusters but also from mid- and small-budget romance and horror titles, pointing to a wider range of genres and scales among successful local releases. Premium-format screenings continued their growth streak, generating KRW45.7 billion ($31.5 million) in revenue for the first half, up 56.3% year-on-year and accounting for 7.9% of total revenue. The council said the trend has climbed steadily since the pandemic as theaters lean on premium formats to differentiate their offerings. The average ticket price for the first half rose KRW551 (¢38) year-on-year to KRW10,150 ($7), reflecting both that shift toward premium formats and higher ticket prices more generally. Showbox Corp. led the distributor rankings, capturing a 48.6% revenue share worth KRW281.4 billion ($194 million) after distributing four releases – “The King’s Warden,” “Colony,” “Salmokji: Whispering Water” and “Once We Were Us” – that all performed well. The Walt Disney Company Korea placed second, taking a 13.8% share worth KRW43.1 billion ($29.7 million) across nine titles that included “Avatar: Fire and Ash,” “Toy Story 5” and “The Devil Wears Prada.” In the independent and arthouse segment, “Backrooms” led the category, taking in KRW12.4 billion ($8.5 million) from 1.16 million admissions. “Ran 12.3” placed second, with “My Name” rounding out the top three. title: ‘The Devil’s Mouth’ Review: Cave Swimmers Become Chum in a Shark Thriller With Extra Claustrophobia
full_text: Jul 29, 2026 3:39am PT ‘The Devil’s Mouth’ Review: Cave Swimmers Become Chum in a Shark Thriller With Extra Claustrophobia Kathryn Newton and Lana Condor headline a generic but watchable Prime Video release made slightly more interesting by toxic friendship dynamics among the human bait. By Guy Lodge Plus Icon Guy Lodge Film Critic @guylodge Latest ‘The Devil’s Mouth’ Review: Cave Swimmers Become Chum in a Shark Thriller With Extra Claustrophobia 35 minutes ago ‘Pinocchio: Unstrung’ Review: Killer Puppetry Is the Best Thing About This Killer Puppet Slasher 3 days ago ‘Bad Counselors’ Review: A Stealthily Christian Comedy Makes Believers of Two Rowdy Frat Bros 4 days ago See All Courtesy of Prime Video “Under Paris,” “Deep Water,” “Thrash,” “Chum” — the shark movies come so thick and fast these days, there’s scarcely any time between them to deem it safe to go back in the water. That said, if this recent run of films is to be believed, regular old beaches are fine these days. Seems the toothy predators are increasingly seeking less obvious locations to graze on wet human flesh: a mid-Pacific plane-crash site, the City of Lights, and now, in “The Devil’s Mouth,” a dark, dank, tight-squeeze cave in idyllic coastal Thailand. This claustrophobic danger zone brings a smidge of novelty to director Jeff Wadlow ‘s aquatic thriller, but the formula is otherwise familiar: five hot young things on vacation, one bull shark very much in business mode, and a pecking order that most viewers can guess five minutes in. Related Stories Peacock to Be Included in YouTube Premium Subscription Bundle Starting in 2027 Anurag Kashyap, Vikramaditya Motwane Present Ravi Muppa's 'Incognito' as New YouTube Shorts Channel Launches (EXCLUSIVE) It’s odd that the shark movie has lately joined the romantic comedy in the ranks of genres most favored for straight-to-streaming fodder, since its pleasures, from “Jaws” onwards, have traditionally been communal, cinematic ones: From the safety of your sofa, a great white jump scare just doesn’t land in quite the same way. A Prime Video release, “The Devil’s Mouth” sometimes feels ill-suited to the small screen, given the frequently squint-inducing murkiness of its setting; on the other hand, the very lax progression of Aja Gabel and Myung Joh Wesner’s Black List-featured script feels tailored to the requirements of second-screen viewing, with character tensions brewing slowly and repetitively between sporadic feeding frenzies. Popular on Variety If the dialogue and characterization never rise above the pedestrian, however, those tensions do at least bring some malicious rooting interest to the essential survival drama — with a strain of toxic friction evident from the get-go between nice-girl protagonist Sarah ( Kathryn Newton ) and her narcissistic BFF Max ( Lana Condor ), a self-declared “CEO of fun,” on their luxury post-graduation vacation. Both stars are better than their thin roles require them to be, with Condor clearly enjoying an opportunity to spike her wholesome “To All the Boys” star persona a bit; perhaps her young fans will resist how blatantly the film’s sympathies are stacked in Sarah’s favor. Or perhaps not: Sarah has a pretty rough time of it from the start. The unpaired fifth wheel on what is otherwise a lovey-dovey couples’ trip — with Max and mutual college friend Adrienne (Tommi Rose) accompanied by their respective, equally bland boyfriends James (Nico Hiraga) and Greg (Gavin Casalegno) — Sarah is quite literally an afterthought when, at the end of a day’s yacht hire in a picturesque cove, the other four set sail while she’s still in the water, leaving her at the mercy of a smack of jellyfish. Cue an initial sea-creature attack less bloody than those to come, but perhaps the film’s most eerily and alarmingly constructed setpiece. A cursory apology from Max (“I’m trying to be accountable here,” she says, unconvincingly) doesn’t quite smooth the waters between the two by the time of the group’s next adventure: a remote coastal cave-swimming expedition led by local guide Wat (“The White Lotus” star Tayme Thapthimthong). A cautionary-tale tone soon sets in as the entitled Americans, led by Max, repeatedly overrule Wat’s native expertise. (The safer cave route he recommends is marked on the map in green; the one they choose is marked in red. How many more flags do you need?) You can hardly blame him for leaving them to their fate when, several caves in, ravaged remains float to the surface, followed in short order by the dreaded fin slicing through the water. How did the beast find its way into these cramped quarters? “I don’t think this is something we need to figure out right now,” says one of the guys, and fair enough, even if that rather lets the screenwriters off the hook. A more immediate priority is navigating a route out of this cave network, with the shark, given limited room to roam, tailing them at every turn. Needless to say, not everyone’s going to make it out alive. The panic-inducing narrowness of the potential escape routes make a change from the genre’s usual spatial dynamics, with Wadlow — recycling some of the atmospherics from his 2020 “Fantasy Island” film, minus the fantasy — and DP James Kniest exploiting those most effectively in a couple of extended, suitably suffocating underwater setpieces. It’s the shark’s appearances, surprisingly, that lack bite. Denied a point of view or much in the way of a closeup, the CG killer never feels a particularly distinctive or palpable presence, while its lunges take on a fairly predictable pattern. The gore, meanwhile, is unexpectedly discreet, which is a strange place for the film to exercise subtlety: A washed-up sea turtle with a cartoon-style bite taken out of it is the most visceral sight here, and the most saddening. The human bait, on the other hand? Have your fill, buddy. ‘The Devil’s Mouth’ Review: Cave Swimmers Become Chum in a Shark Thriller With Extra Claustrophobia Reviewed online, July 28, 2026. Producers: Basil Iwanyk, Erica Lee, Jeff Wadlow. Executive producers: Carsten H.W. Lorenz, Will Flynn, Sam Greenberg. Crew: Director: Jeff Wadlow. Screenplay: Aja Gabel, Myung Joh Wesner. Camera: James Kniest. Editor: Sean Albertson. Music: Bear McCreary. With: Kathryn Newton, Lana Condor, Gavin Casalegno, Nico Hiraga, Tommi Rose, Tayme Thapthimthong. Goodbye, Stars Hollow. title: Korean Box Office Up 42% In 2026 H1, Driven By ‘The King’s Warden’ & Other Local Hits; ‘Project Hail Mary’ Tops Imports
full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz Netflix Sets Awards-Qualifying Theatrical Release For Lee Chang-dong’s Venice & Toronto Title ‘Possible Love’ Prime Video Inks Multi-Year Deal With CJ ENM Bringing More Than 100 Korean Shows To India Hong Kong International Film Festival Society Appoints Fred Tsui As Executive Director View All July 29, 2026 3:01am The King's Warden Showbox South Korea clocked a 41.9% increase in box office revenue in the first half of 2026, according to figures released today by the Korean Film Council (KOFIC), driven by local hits including The King’s Warden , Colony and Salmokji: Whispering Water . KOFIC figures reveal that overall box office from January to June 2026 reached $396.6M (KRW579BN), compared to $279M (KRW408BN) in the same period last year. Admissions also increased during the period – up by 34.2%, compared to the first half of last year, to reach an encouraging 57 million. Korean films powered the recovery with a whopping 81.7% year-on-year increase in revenue to $254M (KRW370.2BN) and a 74.9% increase in admissions to 37.37 million. Related Stories Agencies Artists First Signs 'Project Hail Mary's James Ortiz News Hong Kong Box Office Up 25% In 2026 First Half Topped By Local Hit 'Night King' Compared to pre-pandemic levels, revenue for Korean films recovered to 94.2% of the average during the first halves of 2017–2019 (KRW392.9BN). Korean films also accounted for a 63.9% market share of overall revenue and 65.5% in admissions. Watch on Deadline The King’s Warden , Jang Hang-jun’s period drama starring Yoo Hae-jin, Park Ji-hoon and Yoo Ji-tae, topped the first half year box office with $111.7M (KRW163.1BN) from 16.9 million ticket sales, also becoming the highest-grossing Korean film of all time. It’s also the first Korean title in two years to cross the 10 million admissions benchmark and is second of all time in terms of admissions behind The Admiral: Roaring Currents . Korean films also took the number two and three positions in the first half year chart – Yeon Sang-ho’s zombie thriller Colony , which premiered in Cannes Midnight Screenings, grossed $41M (KRW60.5BN) while low-budget horror Salmokji: Whispering Water pulled in $22.8M (KRW33.3BN). Foreign films saw a 2.3% increase in revenue during the January-June period, with a combined $143M (KRW208.8BN), but ticket sales decreased by 6.9% to 19.68 million. Project Hail Mar y was the highest-grossing import with $22.6M (KRW33BN) followed by Avatar: Fire And Ash and Michael . A24’s Backrooms was the highest-grossing indie film among both local and foreign releases with $8.5M (KRW12.4BN) in revenue and 1.16 million admissions. KOFIC figures also revealed the growing importance of special format screenings with revenue from brands including IMAX, 4D, ScreenX and Dolby Cinema increasing by 56.3% year-on-year to $31.3M (KRW45.7bn) and powering a big chunk of the box office for Avatar: Fire And Ash and Project Hail Mary . Korean studio Showbox, which released all of the top three films, was the biggest distributor during the period with a 48.6% market share, followed by Disney which ranked second with a 13.8% market share. title: Kavinsky, French Producer and DJ Behind ‘Drive’ Opening Song ‘Nightcall,’ Dies at 50
full_text: Jul 29, 2026 2:52am PT Kavinsky, French Producer and DJ Behind ‘Drive’ Opening Song ‘Nightcall,’ Dies at 50 By Elsa Keslassy Plus Icon Elsa Keslassy International Correspondent @elsakeslassy Latest Kavinsky, French Producer and DJ Behind ‘Drive’ Opening Song ‘Nightcall,’ Dies at 50 1 hour ago Canal+ Group’s Revenue Jumps 40% as MultiChoice Deal Boosts Earnings and Subscriptions 20 hours ago Canal+ Seals Landmark Pact to Invest Nearly $1.1 Billion in French and European Films 2 days ago See All Getty Images Kavinsky , the French electro music producer and DJ whose hypnotic anthem “Nightcall” became a cult classic after opening Nicolas Winding Refn’s 2011 film “ Drive ,” died on Tuesday. He was 50. The artist was found dead at his Paris home on Tuesday evening. Authorities have opened an investigation into the circumstances of his death, though no foul play has been reported. French media said the musician had complained of headaches in the days leading up to his death, according to Reuters . Related Stories YouTube Ad Sales Keep Growing at Healthy Clip, Rising 13% to $11 Billion in Q2 Anurag Kashyap, Vikramaditya Motwane Present Ravi Muppa's 'Incognito' as New YouTube Shorts Channel Launches (EXCLUSIVE) While Kavinsky had long been a respected figure on France’s electronic music scene, “Nightcall” transformed him into an international cult favorite. Produced with Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo of Daft Punk and featuring vocals from Lovefoxxx of Brazilian band CSS, the song helped define the film’s aesthetic and became one of the signature electronic tracks of the 2010s. Popular on Variety Kavinsky most recently performed the song alongside Phoenix and Angèle at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games closing ceremony, which was broadcast globally, introducing it to new audiences over a decade after “Drive’s” release. Born Vincent Belorgey in Seine-Saint-Denis in 1975, he came to music relatively late after first working as an actor and appearing in films by longtime friend Quentin Dupieux. Inspired by 1980s action movies, arcade games and sports cars, he developed the fictional persona of Kavinsky, a mysterious, undead driver said to have returned from a fatal Ferrari crash to make electronic music. He emerged in the mid-2000s through the influential French label Record Makers, releasing the EPs “Teddy Boy,” “1986” and “Nightcall” before touring alongside artists including Daft Punk and Justice. His debut album “OutRun,” released in 2013, expanded on the retro-futuristic sound that would become synonymous with the growing synthwave movement. After a long hiatus, he returned with a second album, “Reborn,” in 2022. Although he never achieved the mainstream commercial profile of fellow French electro artists such as Daft Punk or Justice, Kavinsky had a large influence on a generation of producers drawn to nostalgic, cinematic electro music, and helped popularize the synthwave genre well beyond France. title: Kavinsky Dies: French DJ Whose ‘Nightcall’ Track Opened Nicolas Winding Refn’s ‘Drive’ Was 50
full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Kavinsky Dies: French DJ Whose ‘Nightcall’ Track Opened Nicolas Winding Refn’s ‘Drive’ Was 50 Michelle Yeoh EP’d Martial Arts Picture ‘Nak Muay’ Co-Starring Suablack, Buakaw & Saenchai To Begin Filming In Thailand On August 2 Georgia Native Danny McBride To Be Honored With Rome Int’l Film Fest’s Flannery O’Connor Award View All July 29, 2026 2:22am Kavinsky performs during the closing ceremony of Paris 2024 Summer Paralympic Games Michael Reaves/Getty Images French DJ Kavinsky , who was best known internationally for his ‘ Nightcall ’ track which opened Nicolas Winding Refn ’s 2011 film Drive , has died at the age of 50. French media reported that the music artist, producer and DJ was found dead at his home in Paris on Tuesday evening (July 28). The Paris Prosecutors Office said in a statement said that an investigation had been opened into the cause of his death, noting that “first responders found no suspicious elements at the scene”. Born Vincent Belorgey in Paris on July 31, 1975, Kavinsky was a key figure in the French Touch electro music scene alongside the likes of Daft Punk. Related Stories News 'The Odyssey' Scores $21M+ Record Tuesday For Christopher Nolan; 2nd U.S. Weekend Could Top 'Dark Knight' Pics - Box Office News Charles Gaines Dies: 'Pumping Iron' Author Who Helped Launch Arnold Schwarzenegger Was 84 He achieved worldwide fame with his 2010 ‘Nightcall’ track after Winding Refn used it for his 2011 film Drive starring Ryan Gosling opposite Carey Mulligan as a Hollywood stunt driver moonlighting as a getaway driver. Watch on Deadline Kavinsky had released the track – produced by Daft Punk’s Guy-Manuel de Homem-Chriso – the previous year. His cinema connections preceded the Drive breakout through his long collaborative friendship with musician and DJ turned director Quentin Dupieux. He starred under his real name in Dupieux’s medium-length 2002 work Nonfilm , as the actor-protagonist who wakes up to find himself on a surreal film set, and also appeared in Dupieux’s first feature Steak (2007), which also featured his music. More recently, he made a cameo appearance i n Netflix French-language original Banger opposite Vincent starring Vincent Cassel as a jaded DJ. Across his career, Kavinsky released two albums: ‘OutRun’ in 2013 and ‘Reborn’ in 2022. OutRun was created around the concept of a young man who crashes his red Ferrari Testarossa in 1986 and reappears in 2006 as zombie producer, with Kavinsky citing 1980s video games, Miami Vice and the films of Dario Argento as influences. Kavinsky’s recent musical engagements include performing at the closing ceremony of the Paris 2024 Summer Games as part of a celebration of French electronic music at the Stade de France. At the time of his death, he was scheduled to perform at events in France, Mexico and L.A. in the coming months. title: FIFA Under Fire Over Plan To Sell World Cup Stake To Joshua Kushner Investment Firm
full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse FIFA Under Fire Over Plan To Sell World Cup Stake To Joshua Kushner Investment Firm Banijay Entertainment H1 Revenues Dip Slightly In First Earnings Update Since All3Media Deal ‘Blast’ & ‘Idhayam Murali’ Actress Preity Mukhundhan Lands IMDb Breakout Star Award View All July 29, 2026 2:18am UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin, President Donald Trump and FIFA boss Gianni Infantino Getty Controversial plans to sell stakes in the FIFA World Cup to private investors have sparked a furious response from football authorities and politicians. UEFA , the body that governs European football, took the unprecedented step of releasing a statement condemning FIFA’s plan, which involves creating a new entity that would house the commercial rights to its men’s and women’s tournaments. The World Cup “is not FIFA’s to sell,” said UEFA. JP Morgan Chase, the bank that financed the failed breakaway European Super League in 2021, is working with FIFA to create the business, which is being valued at around $20B, per various reports. Though the World Cup is not a commercial enterprise, the formation of FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) would allow it to be exploited by private investors. Related Stories News Noah Kahan Calls Out Donald Trump's Administration For Using "American Cars" Song In White House Social Media Post News Judge Says Donald Trump Can Amend Complaint In Defamation Lawsuit Against The New York Times FIFA confirmed the plan to create FFE and said it would be the controlling shareholder, but the controversial governing body hopes to raise $4.2B by “carefully selecting long-term investors who will purchase minority, non-controlling interests.” Watch on Deadline Thrive Capital, an investment firm led by Joshua Kusher, the brother of President Donald Trump ‘s son-in-law, Jared Kushner, has been approached about investing, it is reported. We have contacted Thrive for comment. Investigations in the Financial Times and The Times newspapers first revealed the FFE plan, which comes on the back of the recent World Cup. New UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham was among notable names slamming FFE, writing that the World Cup is “not a product, and that “once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out.” Even Sepp Blatter, the disgraced predecessor of FIFA President Gianni Infantino , wrote on social media: “The close relationship between the FIFA President and the US President has reached a financial dimension that is deeply damaging football. No one has the right to sell our game.” Under-fire FIFA President Infantino stands to personally make millions from the deal by becoming its commissioner after his expected third term at football’s governing body expires in 2031, the Times reported. We have contacted FIFA for comment. Infantino said FFE would see “the commercial side of the game [operate] as a focused, dedicated business, with its value shared more and better all around the world,” with FIFA claiming more than $10B would be redistributed back to its 211 member associations following the deals. The recent World Cup in the U.S., Canada and Mexico was heavily criticized in some quarters for the implementation of mandatory drinks breaks, which effectively divided matches into quarters rather than the traditional halves, for Trump’s intervention into the suspension of USMNT player Folarin Balogun and the extended half-time break in the final to allow for musical performances. UEFA President Aleksander Čeferin boycotted the final in response to the various issues. FIFA made record revenues from the tournament, which it has touted publicly. Critics say finances are being put before the best interests of the game. UEFA considers World Cup boycott It has been reported today that UEFA members are meeting to discuss their response to FIFA’s plan, with a boycott of the World Cup one serious option on the table. While UEFA cannot stop it moving ahead, it is the strongest continental body in football with many of the world’s top international teams hailing from the continent. Of the eight quarter finalists at the World Cup, six were UEFA members, and Spain won the tournament. There were similar statistics in the 2018 and 2022 tournaments, and a World Cup without European participation would be a huge commercial and political hit to FIFA. The next World Cup is due to be held in Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with other games held in South America. In its statement in response to FFE, UEFA said: “This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross. UEFA takes it extremely seriously. The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade – especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA’s to sell.” European dominance of world football has been a sore point for many years, and the Swiss-born Infantino has consolidated his power base by redirecting more funding and support to Africa, the Americas and Asia. It is expected that FFE would need to be ratified by a majority of FIFA members, though there’s no word on when or how the vote will take shape. title: FIFA Faces Revolt Over $20B World Cup Sell Off Plan
full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All July 29, 2026 2:01am FIFA President Gianni Infantino and U.S. President Donald Trump at the final of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Alex Livesey - Danehouse/Getty Images World soccer governing body FIFA and its controversial CEO Gianni Infantino are under fire over plans to sell off a stake in FIFA’s commercial operations to private equity investors. The plan would see FIFA set up a new entity, called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), that would bundle all the money-making operations associated with the soccer World Cup — including broadcast rights, sponsorship, ticket sales and licensing fees — and sell a significant stake in the new operation to private investors. FIFA is valuing the new commercial venture at around $20 billion. Thrive Capital, an investment company founded by Joshua Kushner, brother of Donald Trump ’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, is leading the search for investors. The backlash was immediate. European soccer governing body UEFA condemned the plan, saying the sport “isn’t FIFA’s to sell.” “This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross,” UEFA said in a statement. “The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade — especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially.” U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham joined the fray, taking to social media to post that “football does not belong to investors. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never… — Andy Burnham (@andyburnham) July 28, 2026 FIFA says the FFE could raise an additional $10 billion for its member organizations, the 211 national soccer leagues that make up the association. If members approve the plan, FIFA said it could more than double funding to its member associations from $8 million to $20 million a year, a huge sum for the majority of FIFA members. Infantino defended the plan as a way to spread the wealth generated by the World Cup globally. “This is about the democratization of football worldwide,” he said in a statement. Others see a money grab. FIFA and Infantino have been sharply criticized for the commercialization of the recent World Cup , held in the U.S., Canada and Mexico. FIFA expanded the event from 32 to 48 teams, greatly increasing the number of games, allowed a pricey resale market for tickets, and introduced controversial “hydration breaks” which stopped play and allowed for additional advertising during matches. The 2026 tournament was the most lucrative in history, with FIFA expected to announce revenues of more than $15 billion for the event. Given Joshua Kushner’s connection, via his brother, to President Trump, many also see a potential political conflict of interest. Infantino already has close ties to the U.S. President. After Trump complained about not winning the Nobel Peace Prize, Infantino invented the “FIFA Peace Prize” and then awarded it to POTUS in December. UEFA claims FIFA undermined the integrity of this year’s World Cup when it intervened to overturn a red card given to USA striker Falorin Balogun after Trump called and asked Infantino to do so. This week, Jamie Raskin, the top Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, launched an investigation into Infantino and FIFA’s ties to Trump’s administration and businesses. THR

title: ‘Bloody Tennis,’ Tunisian Horror and a Surgeon With Kleptomania: Quirky Films at Locarno
full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All July 29, 2026 2:00am 'Bloody Tennis' Courtesy of augenschein Filmproduktion The Locarno Film Festival , whose 79th edition takes place Aug. 5-15, always features world premieres from around the world by established and up-and-coming auteurs, new hidden gems and cinematic discoveries, along with highlights from the festival circuit. But audiences can also expect the unexpected. After all, Locarno also features quirky, edgy and offbeat movies just waiting to unspool. So, buckle up for a ride on the wilder and more unorthodox side of the cinematic spectrum as THR presents its look at some of the more unusual-sounding films at Locarno79. Related Stories TV 'Babylon Berlin' Sets Finale Date, Unveils Video Game, Documentary, Audio Spinoffs Movies New Mike Leigh, Pablo Larrain Films in San Sebastian Competition Wandering Trees ( Alberi erranti ) Director: Salvatore Section: International competition ‘Wandering Trees,’ courtesy of Locarno Film Festival Once upon a time in Sardinia. Piero and his son Giuliano lived alone in a farmhouse filled with injured animals that they cared for. But the local notables wanted to drive them out because they lived like vagrants. One day, snow fell, and Piero disappeared, while the animals were killed. So, Giuliano had no choice but to search for his father. On his journey, he met Maddalena, and it was love at first sight. Giuliano’s dreamlike search across a wounded landscape explores the wonder and special experience of childhood, a time in life that provides a possibility of resistance against the violence of the adult world. The filmmaker puts it into magical images – and words. “To tell a love story, you mustn’t be afraid to open up emotionally,” says Mereu, who also wrote the script with Alberto Capitta, in a director’s note. “But to embark on a fairy tale, you need to risk something. When you accept its rules, you have to accept everything – even the unthinkable.” Objet A Director: Ann Oren Section: International competition ‘Object A’ Courtesy of Juan Sarmiento G./Schuldenberg Films Ready for a bold, playful and stylized excursion into fragile relationships between humans as well as humans and nature, intimacy, desire, identity – and kleptomania – that uses the body as the core of its cinematic language? Well, Objet A is ready to bend your mind and leave you unsettled! “Ingeborg and Adam are visionary hand surgeons bound by love, control and irresistible fixations,” teases a synopsis. But there is more: “She is compelled to steal objects; he longs to become one. When an accident brings the enigmatic Gaia into their lives, unexpected desires begin to take shape, unsettling the careful balance that has long defined their relationship.” Berlin-based visual artist and filmmaker Ann Oren ( Piaffe ) returns to Locarno to serve up a film, which she wrote with Geoffroy Grison, that features cinematography by Juan Sarmiento G. ( The Voice of Hind Rajab , A Poet ) and editing by Hansjörg Weißbrich ( Rose , Late Shift ). It stars Aenne Schwarz ( All Is Well , Every You Every Me ) as Ingeborg, Louis Hofmann ( All the Light We Cannot See , The Forger , Dark ), and Simone Bucio ( Piaffe , The Ivy ) as Gaia. “I’m interested in human desire and how it connects us to other species,” Oren says in a director’s note. “The human body is the starting point for my cinematic language: the more control we have over it, the more we separate ourselves from the natural world.” Bloody Tennis Director: Nikias Chryssos Section: Out of competition ‘Bloody Tennis,’ courtesy of augenschein Filmproduktion The world of elite sports is taken to disturbing new heights full of brutality and painful ambition in the new film from Nikias Chryssos ( The Bunker , Rave On , A Pure Place ). “Sophie joins a prestigious tennis academy where the brutality of competitive sports is taken to its extreme, and only the hungriest survive,” warns a synopsis. Sandra Guldberg Kampp ( Assassin’s Creed , Electric Child ), Helena Zengel ( News of the World , The Legend of Ochi , System Crasher ) and others star in the movie, along with Elina Löwensohn ( Schindler’s List ), and Zlatko Burić ( Triangle of Sadness ), with an original score by Jim Williams ( Titane , Raw ). If that’s not enough for you yet, the press notes also promise, or should that be: threaten, “blood-sucking leeches, hard-hitting serves and delicious nightmares.” Game on! Bakma Abdelhamid Bouchnak Section: Out of competition ‘Bakma,’ courtesy of Chams Ghorab You have surely never seen Tunisia like this. And you likely haven’t seen a film from Tunisia like this before. What Bouchnak unleashes onto Locarno screens is an urban horror thriller, which he also wrote and edited, with cinematography by Chams Ghorab. Animalistic violence takes on a different meaning in this movie. Commissioner Ali and Khaled investigate the ritualistic murder of a young woman. So far, so horrible. But there is more, as a synopsis highlights: “Her limbs have been severed, her head is missing, and in its place, the killer has grotesquely sewn the head of a dog.” Locarno artistic director Giona A. Nazzaro, in unveiling this year’s festival lineup, highlighted said about Bakma : “It’s a film that, in a very specific way, addresses the political corruption in Tunis at the moment. It’s also a very bitter commentary on what’s left of the so-called Arab Spring that ignited the overthrow of some regimes – and, as you’ll remember, it originated in Tunis.” Tomorrow a Long Time Ago ( Morgen vor langer Zeit ) Director: Luise Donschen Section: Filmmakers of the Present Competition Not much dialogue is used, or needed, in the new film from Donschen ( Casanovagen ), which stars Gerti Drassl and Manuela Biedermann and others. After all, life and actions say more than words. Amid German reunification in 1990, the 50-year-old Patty first loses her job and then her friend Jelena. “In a small East German town, she collects discarded objects and meets the younger Franz,” teases a synopsis. “When her flat becomes so full of belongings that she can no longer enter it, she sets out into a colorful forest. A journey through landscapes and history begins, carrying away more than just her.” The movie has a personal dimension for the filmmaker who grew up in the GDR. “Inspired by my childhood experience of German reunification, the film captures the moment when the present splits into ‘before’ and ‘after’,” the moment when everything seems completely unseen and very familiar at the same time.” Donkey Princess ( Princesa Burro ) Directors: Cristóbal León and Joaquín Cociña Section: International competition ‘Donkey Princess’ Courtesy of Benjamin Echazarreta Once upon a time… wait a second, isn’t that how we started this journey into the mind- and genre-bending films at Locarno79!? But wait, this one is different, although love plays a key role again. Diana is the princess of an ancient kingdom. Her father, King Arthur, has forbidden love. So, when Diana falls in love with Lalo, the King banishes him. A synopsis teases where things go from here: “Using a magical bracelet, Diana travels to other worlds in search of her love. Discovering that her father manipulates her decisions, she must face her fears and change her destiny.” The travels of the protagonist allow the director duo to play with the look and feel of the places she visits. “Diana travels through parallel worlds where each universe transforms the film’s genre,” León and Cociña explain. “The film brings this constant mutation of realities into live action, where fantasy reshapes everything.” So, who’s ready for a cinematic trip!? THR

Disruptive Element Films – Krishnan’s UK and Thailand-based joint company with Colin Pons – has announced an August 2 start for principal photography, with filming due to take place on location in Bangkok and the rural district of Pranburi. It is the third feature for medic-turned director Krishnan, who broke out with Bafta-winning short Showscan , and has since taken directing credits on TV shows such as A Thousand Blows , The Mosquito Coast , Industry , WeCrashed as well as features Been So Long and Junkhearts . As Thailand’s undefeated Muay Thai champion, he is a national icon, the face of global brands, and a fixture in Bangkok’s elite circles. Cinematography will be by Gavin Kelly ( American Horror Story ). Yeoh ( Everything Everywhere All At Once , Crouching Tiger Hidden Dragon ) is also on board as an executive producer alongside Pons, Krishnan and David Ismalone. The film is being shot and produced entirely in Thailand with support from the Thai government and the UK Global Screen Fund. title: Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Rajasthan Royals Sales Push IPL Cricket’s Business Value to $20.6 Billion, Houlihan Lokey Study Finds
full_text: Jul 29, 2026 12:00am PT Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Rajasthan Royals Sales Push IPL Cricket’s Business Value to $20.6 Billion, Houlihan Lokey Study Finds By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest BTS Won’t Submit for 2027 Grammy Awards Consideration 4 hours ago Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Rajasthan Royals Sales Push IPL Cricket’s Business Value to $20.6 Billion, Houlihan Lokey Study Finds 4 hours ago How Lan Hongchun’s Teochew Film ‘Dear You’ Turned a Forgotten Postal Tradition Into China’s Unlikely Hit: ‘Dialect Is Never Going to Be a Liability as Long as You Have Great Ideas’ 20 hours ago See All Getty Images The Indian Premier League cricket tournament’s business value has climbed to $20.6 billion, up 11.4% year over year, according to Houlihan Lokey’s 2026 IPL Valuation Study released Wednesday, as record-setting sales of Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Rajasthan Royals reset franchise pricing across the league. The league’s stand-alone brand value rose 10.3% to $4.3 billion, marking a second consecutive year of double-digit growth for both metrics. The report placed the 2026 figures in historical context: the IPL’s business value stood at $15.4 billion in 2023, $16.4 billion in 2024 and $18.5 billion in 2025. On a per-match basis, Houlihan Lokey noted, only the NFL ranks ahead of the IPL globally. Related Stories Peacock to Be Included in YouTube Premium Subscription Bundle Starting in 2027 Anurag Kashyap, Vikramaditya Motwane Present Ravi Muppa's 'Incognito' as New YouTube Shorts Channel Launches (EXCLUSIVE) The 2026 season’s defining commercial event was the sale of two franchises. Royal Challengers Bengaluru was acquired in March by a consortium including the Aditya Birla Group, the Times of India Group, David Blitzer’s Bolt Ventures and Blackstone’s BXPE for $1.78 billion, the most expensive single IPL franchise transaction on record. The deal, in an all-cash structure, came after seller United Spirits Limited had targeted $2 billion. Rajasthan Royals followed in May, sold to the Mittal family and Serum Institute of India CEO Adar Poonawalla for $1.65 billion, after an initial agreement with a U.S.-based consortium led by Kal Somani collapsed during exclusivity. Together the two deals total $3.43 billion. Popular on Variety “The most telling development this year did not come from our models; it came from the market. Two franchises changed hands – Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) for $1.78 billion and Rajasthan Royals (RR) for $1.65 billion – and the buyers, from Blackstone and the Aditya Birla Group to ArcelorMittal, the Serum Institute, and the global sports investor David Blitzer, are precisely the caliber of capital we have long argued the league was built to attract,” said Harsh Talikoti, director in Houlihan Lokey’s financial and valuation advisory business. The report found viewership undergoing what it called a platform migration rather than a decline. Total reach across television and digital hit 1.06 billion screens, up 7% year over year, even as linear television ratings fell 18.8% and average per-match viewership on television dropped 26%. Total IPL 2026 revenue projections, including broadcasting rights, sponsorships and ticket sales, exceed $1.8 billion. At the franchise level, RCB topped both the brand value and business value rankings for the first time in league history, its brand worth rising 16% to $312 million on the strength of back-to-back IPL and Women’s Premier League titles. Mumbai Indians ranked second at $264 million despite a ninth-place finish, while Kolkata Knight Riders overtook Chennai Super Kings for the No. 3 brand spot at $245 million. Sunrisers Hyderabad and Rajasthan Royals rounded out the top six, both securing playoff berths, while Lucknow Super Giants finished last on both business and brand value at $122 million following Rishabh Pant’s decision to step down as captain. Satyan Gajwani, co-owner of Royal Challengers Bengaluru and chair of Times Internet, said the franchise’s fan engagement drove the acquisition decision. “RCB’s fanbase intensity and connection are unparalleled, which made this a special opportunity,” Gajwani said. Ness Wadia, co-owner of Punjab Kings and one of the league’s founding investors since 2008, said the IPL remains in its early stages of growth. “I still think the IPL is only getting started,” Wadia said. Beyond the headline transactions, the report examined what it described as the league’s structural appeal to private equity relative to other global sports properties. The BCCI places no cap on private equity ownership of an IPL franchise and imposes no minimum hold period, in contrast with the NFL’s 10% per-fund limit, the NBA’s 20% cap and the Bundesliga’s 50+1 rule limiting outside investors to a 49% economic interest. Each franchise also receives roughly $55 million annually from the BCCI’s centrally negotiated media pool before any team-level revenue is counted, a structure the report likened to a contracted annuity. Non-media revenue such as team sponsorships, gate receipts and international expansion is also growing quickly. Houlihan Lokey said non-media revenues have expanded at a 22% compound annual rate since the pandemic, with several IPL owners acquiring stakes in England’s The Hundred, including Reliance Industries’ purchase of a stake in Oval Invincibles and Sun Group’s acquisition of Northern Superchargers. Houlihan Lokey projected the league’s 2028-32 media rights cycle, currently valued at $6.2 billion, could grow by 80% to 100%, citing an uninterrupted 18% compound annual growth rate in rights value since 2008 and expanding international viewership. That estimate cuts against a separate forecast from Media Partners Asia, which projected in a March report that the 2028–32 cycle would instead hold flat at approximately $5.4 billion, with per-match value declining 13%, from $13.2 million to $11.5 million, as the league’s expanded 94-match format dilutes individual game value. title: ‘As Light as Air’ Is a Hypnotic Experimental Doc About Collective Ecstasy in a City in Pakistan (Locarno Trailer)
full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All July 28, 2026 11:59pm 'As Light as Air' Courtesy of Locarno Film Festival As Light as Air is the title of Pakistani filmmaker Umair Bilal’s feature debut, which will world premiere on Aug. 11 in the Critics’ Weeks lineup of the 79th edition of the Locarno Film Festival in Switzerland. But things are not only light but also hypnotic in the cinematic world that the experimental documentary invites people into. After all, it dives into spiritual life in Sehwan, Pakistan, a Sufi city “shaped by pilgrimage, folklore and collective ecstasy,” as the press notes highlight. Sufism is the major expression of mysticism in Islam. Related Stories Business FIFA Faces Revolt Over $20B World Cup Sell Off Plan Movies 'Bloody Tennis,' Tunisian Horror and a Surgeon With Kleptomania: Quirky Films at Locarno “Every day, pilgrims, wanderers, and seekers arrive in a Sufi town carrying grief, hope, and longing,” reads a synopsis on the festival’s website. “Drawn together by music and devotion, they surrender themselves to a shared state of trance.” Bilai also produced the film and handled cinematography together with Konstantin Stell. The editor is Siddhant Sarin, while Sui Sofie Heinz and YANT are responsible for the music. “My connection to the city of Sehwan is personal. My mother followed Sufism and took me to shrines when I was a child, so returning years later carried a distant sense of familiarity,” Bilai shares in a director’s statement. “I was drawn to such places, where people gather to experience states that feel transcendental. In a world that can feel increasingly suffocating, these spaces offer something close to sanctuary, a temporary release from the weight of everyday life.” When he first arrived to film, he approached Sehwan as “an observer, trying to understand the repetitive patterns and rituals that have been followed for centuries,” the filmmaker highlights. “But the space of spirituality felt beyond rationality. By spending long hours with the inhabitants of Sehwan, and allowing myself to move at the town’s own rhythm, I began to let go of that need to understand everything, and instead let myself feel the space. The more I surrendered, the more it revealed itself. Gradually, I became part of its rhythm.” THR can now reveal the trailer for the film. full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse FIFA Under Fire Over Plan To Sell World Cup Stake To Joshua Kushner Investment Firm Banijay Entertainment H1 Revenues Dip Slightly In First Earnings Update Since All3Media Deal ‘Blast’ & ‘Idhayam Murali’ Actress Preity Mukhundhan Lands IMDb Breakout Star Award View All July 28, 2026 11:19pm 'MasterChef' and 'The Traitors' now part of the same group at Banijay Entertainment Fox/BBC Banijay Entertainment’s first financials since its merger with All3Media showed half-year revenues down slightly at €1.37 billion ($1.56 billion), as production volume fell. Sales at the independent European production giant were down 2.2% on the same six months in 2025, which reflected “anticipated phasing in production and distribution.” The numbers do not include All3, whose financials will be included in quarterly reports from Q3. Banijay’s production revenue fell 11.9%, while distribution was up 10.5% “fuelled in particular by a format sale in the first quarter.” Banijay is anticipating numbers to tick up in the second half of the year, with Q4 earmarked for significant activity. Related Stories News Canal+ Posts Big H1 Gains Thanks To $2B Deal For Africa's MultiChoice News Netflix Unveils Live Darts Event With Teenage Sensation Luke Littler Banijay Group groups Banijay Entertainment with its live events business, which saw its revenues zoom up nearly 50% on the back of the Winter Olympic Games and the FIFA World Cup. Watch on Deadline Earlier this month, Banijay merged its entertainment arm with RedBird IMI’s All3Media, creating an $8B revenue giant that Banijay Entertainment Chair Jeff Zucker claims is the largest indie producer ever created. The combined group owns the likes of MasterChef , Big Brother , The Traitors , Peaky Blinders , Midsomer Murders and Gogglebox , and has a library of more than 265,000 hours. Banijay Group received €801M from the deal, including a payment of €625M from RedBird IMI and a €176M pre-closing dividend. The agreement meant Banijay and RedBird IMI have an equal split of the new Banijay Entertainment, which is led by Marco Bassetti as CEO, Jane Turton, former CEO of All3Media, as Deputy CEO, and Zucker, CEO of RedBird IMI, as chair. Banijay announced today that its shareholders would get an exceptional dividend of €400M following the deal, which works out to €0.93 per share. The plan had first been revealed upon announcement of a deal with All3 back in March. Banijay also noted that a seven-year €750M loan secured last month would go towards refinancing All3’s “outstanding” senior facilities, paying transaction fees and paying “certain” dividends related to the merger. At group level, Banijay posted H1 revenues of €2.58B, up 16.9% year-on-year on a reported basis. Adjusted EBITDA was €502.9M, up 18.5%, though adjusted net income fell 3.7% to €141.5M. The sports betting and gaming unit posted revenues only just behind entertainment, coming in at €1.21B. The unit is currently integrating Tipico, which was acquired in a multi-billion dollar deal in October last year, and is in the process of buying France’s second-largest casino operator, JOA. “2026 is definitely a transformational year for Banijay Group,” said Banijay Group CEO Francois Riahi. “The successful acquisition of Tipico, the completion of the combination of Banijay Entertainment and All3Media, and the proposed acquisition of JOA in France grant to the group more scale, more diversity in terms of geography, channels of distribution, and a better strategic positioning to achieve all its strategic goals, creating new opportunities for both growth and value creation.” Jared Leto Accused Of Criminal Sexual Conduct By Four Women In BBC Documentary ‘Brand New Day’ Eyes Huge $465M Global Bow; Review & Red Carpet Pics Ari Emanuel Backs Par-WBD Deal In WSJ Op-Ed, Calls AGs’ Antitrust Suit “Trash” CBS’ Bari Weiss-Led ‘60 Minutes’ Adds Big-Name Correspondents & Contributors Read More About: Comments

title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Swings to China’s Biggest Superhero Opening in Seven Years
full_text: × Skip to main content By Patrick Brzeski Plus Icon Patrick Brzeski Asia Bureau Chief View All July 28, 2026 10:53pm Tom Holland in 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day.' Sony Pictures Could it be that Hollywood’s superheroes have begun to rediscover their powers in China ? Perhaps not yet — but their friendly neighborhood standard-bearer certainly has. Spider-Man : Brand New Day opened across China on Wednesday at a pace the market has not seen for a U.S. comic-book movie in at least seven years, earning more than $16.5 million (RMB 112 million) by midday, with local ticketing giant Maoyan projecting a $37.4 million (RMB 254 million) first-day total. No other superhero title has come close to such heights since Spider-Man: Far From Home bowed to $36 million in 2019. Sitting in a distant second is Venom: The Last Dance with $9.4 million earned on its first day on Chinese screens in 2024. Related Stories Movies 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Review: Tom Holland Bares His Soul in a Superhero Installment That Balances Self-Reflection With Action TV 'Babylon Berlin' Sets Finale Date, Unveils Video Game, Documentary, Audio Spinoffs And Chinese box-office trackers foresee even bigger things for Tom Holland’s latest swing in the spider suit. Maoyan’s full-run forecast, published on the eve of release, pegs the film’s ultimate China total at a whopping $255 million (RMB 1.73 billion), with rival tracker Dengta going higher still at more than $265 million (RMB 1.8 billion). Such projections routinely get revised as a run matures — day-one forecasts especially — but a finish anywhere near that range would rank as Hollywood’s biggest China gross since Avengers: Endgame in 2019, surpassing even Avatar: The Way of Water ‘s $246 million. The Beijing industry has been buzzing all week about Brand New Day ‘s box-office potential. Presales finished at $18.6 million (RMB 126.2 million) — the best of any imported film of the past three summers. The film appears to be benefiting from some pent-up demand for Marvel’s most iconic character. Spider-Man: Far From Home , the last entry to play in Chinese theaters, opened to a strong $98 million over its debut weekend in 2019, finishing at $199 million. That title remains the last U.S. superhero film to clear $100 million in China. Huge sales were expected for its follow-up, the $1.92 billion-grossing Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021), but the film never opened in China after local regulators reportedly balked at the prominence of the Statue of Liberty in the movie’s climax, and Sony declined to cut around it. In the years since, U.S. superhero cinema has fallen out of favor in China even more dramatically than elsewhere. Marvel titles were blocked from the market by regulators from mid-2019 to early 2023, and earnings since the ban have been comparatively withering. Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 ($87 million in 2023) and Venom: The Last Dance ($94 million in 2024) stand as the era’s biggest superhero totals, while nearly all other recent entries have limped to sums in the low teens. Chinese audiences, meanwhile, have transferred their enthusiasm to homegrown blockbusters. But Spider-Man has always stood apart, and Sony and Marvel courted the market accordingly. China was given the world’s earliest release date for Brand New Day — Wednesday’s bow comes two days ahead of North America’s — along with an exclusive Imax launch unavailable to fans in the U.S., where large-format screens remain occupied by Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey . Holland and Zendaya flew to China for last week’s local premiere in Shanghai, where Holland charmed local media with an account of Jackie Chan visiting the film’s London set (the Chinese action icon’s famed stunt team reportedly helped choreograph some of Brand New Day ‘s action sequences). Directed by Shang-Chi ‘s Destin Daniel Cretton, Brand New Day picks up four years after No Way Home , with a forgotten Peter Parker protecting New York alone — and the strain beginning to weigh on him. The film has earned strong reviews from critics , with its Rotten Tomatoes’ score currently hovering around 90 percent. Analysts are projecting a North America opening in the $180 million range for a global launch over $425 million. THR

title: Evan Rachel Wood Says She’s Not Returning for ‘Practical Magic 2’ Because It’s “Not Following the Book”
full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All July 28, 2026 9:07pm Evan Rachel Wood Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images Evan Rachel Wood is sharing the reason she believes she wasn’t asked to return for the upcoming Practical Magic sequel. During a recent interview with Entertainment Tonight , the actress said it doesn’t seem like Practical Magic 2 will be following the book. The sequel was adapted from author Alice Hoffman’s The Book of Magic , which was the follow-up to her first novel Practical Magic . “I read the book and it seems like they’re not following the book,” Wood said. “I think in the book it would have made sense to bring me back; I think in the way they’re redoing it and approaching it, it didn’t make sense.” Related Stories Lifestyle Mena Suvari to Record Audiobook for New Novel From 'Practical Magic' Author Alice Hoffman (Exclusive) Movies Pam Abdy and Sandra Bullock Talk Paramount-Warners Deal and 'Practical Magic 2' The 1998 film followed two witch sisters (played by Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman), raised by their eccentric aunts, as they face a curse that threatens any man who falls in love with an Owens woman. Wood and Alexandra Artrip played the daughters of Bullock’s character, Sally Owens. Earlier this month, Wood took to Instagram to confirm for fans that she wouldn’t be reprising her role in the new film. “I am getting asked about this a lot, so l’ll just clear it up now; I was not asked to come back and be in the Practical Magic sequel,” she wrote at the time. “l offered my services, even if it was one scene or one line. I was told they are recasting. I am sorry to disappoint the fans. It was not in my control or my choice. I would have happily rejoined my sisters.” In the sequel, Joey King was recast to play Wood’s character, while Maisie Williams will be playing the younger sister of Artrip’s character from the first film. Dianne Wiest and Stockard Channing will also be reprising their characters, Aunt Jet and Aunt Franny, respectively. Wood also told ET that she’s “sad” she doesn’t get to return because “we bonded with that cast so much as children, and so to miss out on the opportunity to look at that cast and look at that house as an adult and see the history in our eyes, it’s something that can’t be faked.” Practical Magic 2 hits theaters on Sept. 11.
